01Dashboard SummaryOVERVIEW▶

The starting point for Izzy’s snow thrower push key challenge as Swami ran it with Claude. Two models, Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5, each built a live parametric key generator from the same brief, and a third dashboard compares the two runs. The sections below say what each holds, each with a launch button. Terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

Three dashboardsFable generator: first model in 12m13s, 19 spec issues. Opus generator: first model in about 10 minutes, 22 spec issues, support-free by default. The comparison finds Opus used about 3.5 times less of the 5-hour session.

03The ChallengeBRIEF▶

Izzy set an AI design challenge: one written specification for a replacement snow thrower push key, given to several AI tools and to human engineers to see who returns the cleanest design [4]. The key is a single PETG part with three components: a stem that pushes into the spring-loaded switch, a guard that stops it, and a handle sized for winter gloves with a lanyard hole.

  • Same briefBoth generators were built from the identical prompt, spec, original key photo and skills, in separate threads, at medium thinking. Neither could see the other’s work.
  • Swami’s rulingsDecided up front for both: stem total 33.5 mm, recess on both faces of the stem, single-piece print, export STL and quad OBJ.
  • ThingiverseThe existing two-half Thingiverse model Izzy mentioned was documentation only. Neither generator used it or its photo to make the key.
  • BenchmarkThe spec asks every entrant to log the time from prompt to model and every spec error with its workaround. Both entries carry that log.
  • Not yetNo test print and no native Fusion model so far; both entries are browser generators with mesh export.
PartMain dimensionsFeatures
Stem34 × 9.5 × 4.1 mm (33.5 mm used)Recessed web, 6 mm square locking window, side notch, diamond tip, 0.5 mm chamfers
Guard3 × 18 × 11 mmStop collar with rounded edges
Handle24 × 27 × 17 mm maxGlove-sized grip, ribbed texture, 4.5 mm lanyard hole
Where to startOpen either generator to see and change the key, or open the comparison for the verdict. The full spec is in the Source Document at the bottom of this page.
04Opus 5.5 GeneratorGENERATOR▶
Launch Opus 5.5 generator →

The Snow Thrower Key Generator (Opus) [2] is the Opus 5.5 entry, built at medium thinking from the same brief. Every spec dimension is a live control and the key updates as you change it. Its key design call: a symmetric key with a 17 mm handle cannot print flat in one piece, so by default every part’s underside sits on the bed and the key prints with no supports. An OEM centred option restores the symmetric shape.

  • ViewerPreset views, an orthographic mode, the quad mesh, a section cut, a measuring tool and an overhang check for printing.
  • ControlsGrouped into stem, guard, handle, grip and lanyard, and print settings, with a live mesh check at the top.
  • ExportSTL, quad OBJ and a 3MF with slicer paint, so each part arrives coloured in the slicer.
  • Clean edgesThe plan grid lands exactly on every edge, so nothing is jagged, and the lanyard hole is a true circle.
  • Thingiverse sectionA reference-only section shows the Thingiverse model Izzy mentioned; it was not used.
05Fable 5.2 GeneratorGENERATOR▶
Launch Fable 5.2 generator →

The Snow Thrower Key Generator (Fable) [1] is the Fable 5.2 entry, built at medium thinking. It is a live parametric generator: every spec dimension is a number box and slider, and the 3D key rebuilds as you type. It keeps the original key’s symmetric shape, so the stem floats above the bed and needs supports when printed.

  • ViewerOrbit and zoom, shading modes, mesh lines, a section cut and a two-point measuring tool.
  • Part coloursStem, guard, handle, and grip and lanyard each have their own colour, on the control panel and on the model.
  • ExportSTL for slicing, quad OBJ, a colour 3MF and the parameter table, saved as a zip.
  • Thingiverse sectionA reference section shows the Thingiverse model for the record, marked as not used.
  • SpecThe spec renders as a formatted document, with the raw markdown one click away.
06Opus vs Fable ComparisonCOMPARISON▶
Launch the comparison ↗

The Opus vs Fable Key Run dashboard [3] measures what each run cost and what it produced, using Swami’s usage page readings before and after each run. Fable ran first and Opus second, so the readings split cleanly.

  • Session useOpus used about 4 points of the 5-hour session against about 14 for Fable, roughly 3.5 times less.
  • Weekly useAbout a third of a weekly point for Opus against about 2 for Fable.
  • SpeedOpus reached its first watertight model about two minutes sooner and published about eight minutes sooner.
  • PlasticThe Opus key uses about 19% less plastic (7.24 against 8.93 cm³) and prints without supports.
  • Spec readingClose to a tie: 16 shared topics, with each model catching a few issues the other missed.
  • Fable resetsSwami’s three free Fable resets can refund a Fable run while they last, which narrows the cost gap.
One lineOn this task, Opus 5.5 at medium thinking matched Fable 5.2’s output for roughly 3.5 times less session usage and in about 70% of the time.

09GlossaryREFERENCE▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section. Each term’s Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
Push keyKeyA plastic key pushed straight into the snow thrower’s switch to enable it; no turning.
StemKeyThe flat blade that pushes into the spring-loaded switch barrel.
GuardKeyThe collar between stem and handle that stops the key at the right depth.
Locking windowKeyThe 6 mm square hole in the stem that the switch latches into.
Lanyard holeKeyA 4.5 mm hole in the handle for a tether to the machine.
Parametric generatorBenchmarkA page that rebuilds the key live from its dimensions, so any value can change without remodelling.
Spec issueBenchmarkAn ambiguity, conflict or gap in the spec, logged with the workaround applied, as the benchmark requires.
Medium thinkingBenchmarkThe reasoning effort setting both runs used.
Fable 5.2ModelsThe Claude model that built the first entry.
Opus 5.5ModelsThe Claude model that built the second entry.
5-hour sessionModelsThe rolling plan usage limit that refills five hours after a session starts.
STLFilesThe standard triangle mesh file for 3D printing.
Quad OBJFilesAn OBJ mesh made mostly of four-sided faces, easier to edit in modelling tools.
3MFFilesA print file that can carry colours or paint per part along with the mesh.
WatertightFilesA closed mesh with no holes or open edges, so a slicer can tell inside from outside.
PETGPrintingThe tough, slightly flexible plastic the spec calls for.
SupportsPrintingTemporary printed scaffolding under overhangs; a support-free part prints without them.
Flat undersidePrintingOpus’s default layout: every part’s underside on the bed, so the key prints in one piece without supports.
OEM centredPrintingThe original key’s layout, symmetric about its mid-plane, which needs supports.
ThingiversePrintingA site of shared printable models; its two-half key was shown for the record only.
